summary: Local prototype reviewed against financial identity, initial collector, workspace and update-diff boundaries. 298 emulator rules tests passed, including the user-confirmed active Operator payer compatibility. Operators gain no financial write authority. Not a production deployment approval or a guarantee of a complete rules audit.

findings.check: Expense funding identity on create and funding changes
findings.issue: Baseline accepted four invalid new funding combinations. The local candidate rejects them, preserves unchanged legacy funding, and keeps creator/beneficiary/payer distinct. Production rules remain unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Review the narrow candidate and full CI evidence before separately approving deployment. Do not replay retained live expenses automatically.

findings.check: Initial collection exception and general collector authority
findings.issue: The new initial-beneficiary exception must stay bound to the original unpaid ordinary job, original creator/actor, operation UUID and action time. Existing membership, collector metadata, date and atomic amount checks passed the emulator cases; no later Partner collector escalation is granted.
findings.recommendation: Keep positive and adversarial cases mandatory, including compound-write expression-budget regressions and wrong-parent/recorder/beneficiary/repeated receipt denials.

findings.issue: The existing approved offline authorization model trusts original client action time, which is not tamper-proof. Accepted-limitation tests remain visible and unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Treat this as an existing policy limitation. A server-issued offline authorization design would require separate product/security approval; do not change historical timestamps to hide it.

findings.issue: This scoped review does not establish complete hasOnly/type/size validation for every document field or every legacy backend path. Passing the relevant test suite is not a complete schema-hardening claim.
findings.recommendation: Retain the existing gates and schedule separate schema/size-limit hardening if required; avoid unrelated policy changes in this candidate.
